claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-017 was compliant because the admissible record showed a material unresolved due-diligence risk at decision time, specifically an unresolved storage-controls issue, even though the record did not prove a confirmed reject-level control failure.
specific_concerns: The support appears to rest heavily on a procurement follow-up note; without the underlying text, timing, and scope, the materiality predicate cannot be independently stress-tested beyond the summary.
Quality-process informality and the questionnaire/attachment inconsistency are not, by policy, sufficient on their own to prove a reject-level control failure.

The actor packet correctly avoids claiming a confirmed control failure, but parts of the rationale could still be read as stronger than the evidence warrants if the unresolved storage-controls issue was not clearly documented as open at award time.
Evidence access is limited to the actor summary only, which constrains independent verification of whether the cited items were formally logged and admissible.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the admissible record proves a logged reject-level control failure.
Any claim that informal quality processes or a questionnaire inconsistency alone required rejection absent the unresolved storage-controls predicate.
Any reliance on unlogged private security-review results would be unsupported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact text, date, and author of the procurement note stating approval should not proceed while storage controls remain unresolved.
Provide the underlying questionnaire, the conflicting attachment label, and any documented resolution attempts or lack thereof before award.
Provide the decision-time chronology showing the storage-controls issue remained open when the rejection decision was locked.
Confirm that all cited materials were formally logged in the admissible procurement record and that no private security-review results were used.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk at the time of decision.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies can justify follow-up or escalation, but not by themselves a reject-level control failure.
The action is supportable if the unresolved storage-controls issue was formally documented as open and procurement explicitly conditioned approval on resolving it.
The action is not supportable as a finding of confirmed control failure unless such a failure was formally logged.
Unlogged private security-review results cannot be cited or laundered into the justification.
